title: Does Agglomeration Enhance Property Value?
authors: Crocker Herbert Liu; Chen Zheng; Bing Zhu
eligible_reason: No binary staggered-adoption DiD. Tables 4-16 are transaction-level hedonic regressions of log price per square metre, NOI and cap rate (and lease-level rent) on continuous agglomeration indices (neighbourhood specialization, within-building specialization, BN spillover location quotients) plus time-varying property controls, transaction-year, MSA and REIT FE (zb_issue_regression_dummy_tenant_ran.m), with a Bartik-instrument second stage in Table 7. Table 17 and Figure 3 are REIT event studies of daily abnormal returns around building transactions: event-time dummies (-11..11, end-binned) interacted with high-specialization indicators and with every property characteristic (dummy_didtran*), day and firm FE (zb_issue_regression_dummy_event2.m). The estimand is a characteristic-by-event-time interaction (subgroup-by-treatment interaction with additional characteristic interactions), and REITs experience repeated transaction events.
design_notes: MATLAB scripts; master script copied into 'Word Copy of Master Script.docx' (zb_run_tenant_all.m). Event dummies built in zb_creatdummy_event.m with 60-day end bins.

ineligible_specs_listed.reason: continuous agglomeration regressors with time-varying controls; cross-sectional transactions; Table 7 IV
cross-section of cumulative abnormal returns on continuous indices
event time x high-specialization (and x property characteristics) interactions; repeated REIT events; not a binary staggered adoption
